_doc: Which outside models to ask, and how to reach them. Adding, disabling or re-pointing a channel is a change HERE, never in the code. Copy this file next to your casefile.json to override it for one matter; `lawverbatim consult --registry <path>` overrides it for one run.
_why_a_file: Every value in here rotates. Model names change monthly, a weekly subscription limit runs out mid-round, a vendor renames a flag. Measured on the system this was extracted from: two review CLIs changed their model identifier inside one week, and a document that asserted the old one read as documentation rather than as stale. Configuration rots visibly; code rots silently.

_kinds.cli: A command-line tool you already have installed and already pay for. Needs NO API key: it runs on your existing subscription. This is the DEFAULT kind on purpose - a metered API key is a second bill and a second credential to leak, and for this audience neither is necessary.
_kinds.http: An OpenAI-compatible /chat/completions endpoint. Needs an API key, named here and read from the environment - never written in this file. Off unless you turn it on.
_kinds.delegate: Hand the whole round to a separate review harness if one is installed. Its absence is reported as 'not installed here', never as 'does not exist'.

_retention: 🔴 `retains` is the question a lawyer has to be able to answer and nobody else's harness records: does this vendor keep what you send? It is printed in the plan BEFORE anything is sent, and written to the ledger afterwards. `unknown` is an honest value and prints as a warning, because 'we did not check' must never read as 'no'.
_telemetry: Does the channel report which pages it actually opened? Where it does not, this toolkit derives grounding from the URLs in the answer text instead - and labels it as derived. `false` here makes the report print `not measured`, never `0`. Measured on the source system: a channel that had issued 61 searches printed as one that had issued none, because its count lived under a different key.

codex.label: OpenAI Codex CLI
codex._argv_notes: The prompt goes on STDIN and argv ends with `-`. A positional prompt while something else pipes stdin hangs on 'Reading additional input from stdin...'. `--sandbox read-only` still writes the report, because `-o` is not sandboxed.
codex._search_switch: MEASURED against codex-cli 0.146.0, not recalled. `--search` is a GLOBAL flag and its POSITION is the whole story: `codex --search exec ...` is accepted, `codex exec --search ...` dies with `unexpected argument '--search' found`. Separately, both `-c tools.web_search=true` and `-c web_search="live"` are accepted - two different settings, not two spellings of one. Three outside reviewers split on this exact question and each was partly right; the shell settled it in two seconds. Anything asserted about a flag without running it is a guess wearing a citation.
codex._free_probe: 🔴 A config key can be validated with NO API call and no spend: `codex exec --strict-config -c <key>=<value> -` with empty stdin. An unknown key fails first with `unknown configuration field ... in -c/--config override`; a known key gets past config loading and fails later with `No prompt provided via stdin`. Confirmed with a deliberately bogus control key, because a probe that passes everything proves nothing.
codex._no_model_pinned: No `-m` and no effort override ship here, deliberately. The identifier that was current when this file was written is already wrong by the time you read it, and a wrong `-m` is a hard failure, not a downgrade. Set `model` below to pin one for your machine; leaving it out uses whatever your own config already selects, which is the value you actually maintain.
codex.notes: Strategic questions and line-level audits of a finished draft. Reports no tool telemetry at all, so its grounding is derived from the URLs in its answer.

agy.label: Antigravity CLI (Gemini)
agy._disabled_because: Off by default because its flag set is the one that changes most and a wrong flag here exits non-zero in three seconds. Turn it on once `lawverbatim doctor --channels` reports it green on YOUR machine. Two traps if you do: a permission denial makes it discard the whole run while still exiting 0 with SUCCESS, and `--mode` is unvalidated so it is not the read-only guarantee it looks like.

gemini.label: Gemini CLI
gemini.notes: Enable after doctor confirms it. Kept as a worked example of adding a channel with two lines of JSON and no code.

claude.label: Claude Code CLI
claude._independence_warning: 🔴 If you are already working inside Claude Code, this channel is NOT a second opinion - it is the same model family reading the same files, and its agreement measures nothing. Enable it only as a fourth voice alongside other vendors, never as the reviewer of work it helped write.
claude.notes: Off by default for independence, not for quality.

http.label: Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint
http._key_handling: The key is read from the named environment variable at call time and never written here, never printed, never logged. This file is safe to commit; a file with a key in it is not.
http._metered_warning: 🔴 The only metered kind that ships. If you have a subscription to the same model, use the CLI channel instead: a subscription is several times cheaper than the same tokens through an API, and it cannot run up a bill you did not plan.
http.notes: Off, and needs two environment variables before it will run.

harness.label: A separate multi-model review harness, if installed
harness.notes: If you already run a dedicated orchestration tool, this hands it the same gated brief and then audits everything it brings back. Preferred over the built-in transports when present: it has more channels and better telemetry. When it is absent the built-in CLI channels above still work, so this toolkit is never a dead feature.

_ordering: When `harness` is available it runs INSTEAD of the built-in transports for the channels it covers, not alongside them. Two paths to one vendor would double the spend and produce two answers that look like agreement.

grounding._doc: How to read the URLs a reviewer cites. Domain suffixes, not full domains, so this stays short and portable.
grounding._snapshot_doc: 🔴 An ANNUAL EDITION is a snapshot, not the text in force - and it lives on a .gov domain, so a naive 'is it a government source' check passes it. Measured on the source system: a channel graded clean while grounded on a 2019 CFR edition. These patterns catch the common shapes.
grounding._nonauthoritative_doc: Useful as a lead, never as the source of a legal position. A reviewer that grounds only here has told you where to look, not what the law says.

limits._doc: Ceilings, not targets. A round that hits one of these stops and says so.
